images.title: File:Dülmen, Alte Brennerei Löhning -- 2015 -- 8677-81.jpg
images.author: Dietmar Rabich
images.description: Interior (bottles) of the old distillery Löhning, Dülmen, North Rhine-Westphalia, GermanyThe Löhning distillery was a traditional grain distillery in Dülmen and is a prime example of the long distilling tradition in the Münsterland region.Its origins date back to the 19th century, when many farms began processing surplus grain into grain brandy. The Löhning family also took advantage of this opportunity and developed an independent distillery from a secondary agricultural business. The main product was grain brandy – typical for Westphalia – made from regional rye or wheat.Over the decades, the company modernized its technology, but remained artisanal in character. Like many smaller distilleries, Löhning had to compete with large industrial producers in the 20th century. Thanks to its regional roots, consistent quality, and traditional recipes, the distillery was able to maintain its position in the local market.The Löhning distillery in Dülmen was closed in 1989. The building was then renovated in accordance with historic preservation guidelines and converted into a KfW efficiency house, among other things.

images.title: File:Cardboard Boxes and their History.jpg
images.author: Creativity103
images.description:
Cardboard boxes are industrially prefabricated boxes, primarily used for packaging goods and materials. Specialists in industry seldom use the term cardboard because it does not denote a specific material. 
The term cardboard may refer to a variety of heavy paper-like materials, including card stock, corrugated fiberboard, or paperboard. The meaning of the term may depend on the locale, contents, construction, and personal choice.
In business and industry, material producers, container manufacturers, packaging engineers, and standards organizations, try to use more specific terminology. There is still not complete and uniform usage. Often the term “cardboard” is avoided because it does not define any particular material.
Broad divisions of paper-based packaging materials are:
•	Paper is thin material mainly used for writing upon, printing upon, or for packaging. It is produced by pressing together moist fibers, typically cellulose pulp derived from wood, rags, or grasses, and drying them into flexible sheets.
•	Paperboard, sometimes known as cardboard, is generally thicker (usually over 0.25 mm or 10 points) than paper. According to ISO standards, paperboard is a paper with a basis weight (grammage) above 224 g/m², but there are exceptions. Paperboard can be single- or multi-ply.
•	Corrugated fiberboard sometimes known as corrugated board or corrugated cardboard, is a combined paper-based material consisting of a fluted corrugated medium and one or two flat liner boards.
There are also multiple names for containers:
•	A shipping container made of corrugated fiberboard is sometimes called a "cardboard box", a "carton", or a "case". There are many options for corrugated box design
•	A folding carton made of paperboard is sometimes called a "cardboard box".
•	A set-up box is made of a non-bending grade of paperboard and is sometimes called a "cardboard box".

•	Drink boxes made of paperboard laminates, are sometimes called "cardboard boxes", "cartons", or "boxes".

images.description:
Boxes come all through our lives aimlessly, yet it appears to be come to state that there is dependably an unfaltering supply of them. In the event that you have children who just can’t seem to get rid of those present boxes or need a place to throw out diapers. Perhaps you purchase supplements and stuff from Amazon, or utilize the great AliExpress website. Chances are that the majority of the containers coming all through your home are shipping boxes.
These days, individuals are truly into an easily overlooked detail called "recycling", which is the place you take something that isn't fabulous and you make it more marvellous. (My father would have most likely called this something unique, yet it would be extremely, how do I say it? Nasty to put in a blog entry.) So as opposed to hurling out those delivery boxes, or tossing them on the garbage heap, here are a couple of basic way you can recycle them and utilize them for something else:
Maybe the most astonishing thought for me was making window valances out of cardboard. They looked shockingly beguiling! (On the off chance that you are a window valance sort of person). Envelop them by an overwhelming knitted texture, spruced up with some sparkling brads, and you could never have the capacity to figure the unassuming beginnings.
The most clear approach to upcycle confines is to swing them to better-looking boxes, obviously. Utilize wrapping paper, vellum paper, lace, or peculiar duct tape to fold over the container until the point that it has been totally masked. Paste excellent textures to within and outside, utilizing line to camouflage the corners. On the off chance that that surpasses your skill, envelop them by some rope. The outcomes are stunning.
One of my most loved thoughts is a homework caddy. Take an oat box, a noodle box, and a granola bar box and tape them all together. Remove the tops in amazed statures, and after that in the last box, the most brief and fattest one, put bathroom tissue moves to use for holding pens, markers, and scissors. Utilize vivid conduit tape or paste a pretty strip around it and you could swear it originated from Target.
To wrap things up, it is a developing practice to make real furniture out of cardboard. From headboards to end tables to side tables, from light shades to the window valances I recorded above, you could likely outfit a whole room from transportation boxes. Despite the fact that I would prescribe that you stick to ordinary sleeping pads, for the wellbeing of everybody.
A box can be reconstructed into a basket for you to carry for your next time at the market. Cut the top flaps off of a small Cardboard Boxes . Draw a short line of hot glue along the bottom edge of the box. Quickly press the end of some jute cord into the glue. Continue gluing and wrapping the cord around the box until you reach the top of the box. Trim the excess rope off.

Boxes have an abundance of uses and as you know by now it goes way past using them as make shift dustbins. There’s plenty of DIY's and crafts you can try out using boxes. They can even become those unique, customized items in your house or even be a handy dandy, resourceful little object for you. It does not end just there with boxes you can always unleash your creativity on these boxes and recycle them! Not only will you be doing the environment a huge favour but yourself one too. Spending time on something positive will help you more than you can think.

protocol: Three stratified convenience panels; 20 whole photos each, same predefined object slots. Visually labelled before prediction. Not a random population sample. No trial stopping on successful pictures.
pass_rule: Each panel needs at least 17/20 category AND conditional disposal-route matches; uncertain/manual-review outputs count as failures. Separate category-only accuracy is secondary.
limitations: No claim of unseen foundation-model pretraining. Duplicate checks are heuristic. City of Sydney routes are conditional, not an image-based guarantee of contents or safety. Mixed-items class is not covered.
